hypothesis: Urban/home growers are a core interested segment
rationale: Discourse is overwhelmingly home/hobby scale (PROFESSIONAL_COMMERCIAL signal ~2% of customer voice) and Indonesian videos frequently frame growing at home, on balconies or narrow land. But only ~4% of records state a home/indoor/small-space context explicitly, and SPACE is almost never voiced as a pain. Small space is a usage context, not a recurring frustration.
proposal_action: Keep urban/home growers as the core segment, but frame space as a context ('fits a balcony/terrace') rather than the main problem HYCANE solves.
primary_validation: Screener in primary survey: dwelling type, growing location, available area.

hypothesis: Hydroponic beginners are a core segment with recurring friction
key_metrics: {"metric": "beginner/never-tried among records with an explicit experience signal", "n": 11135, "pct": 84.13, "denominator": 13235, "beginner_problem_solving_pct": 10.87, "nonbeginner_problem_solving_pct": 10.0, "platforms": 8}
rationale: Among records with an explicit experience signal, ~84% are beginner/never-tried, across all 8 platforms; KNOWLEDGE and PLANT_HEALTH are top-5 pains; Indonesian YouTube comments are dominated by how-to questions and learning intent. Caveat: the beginner rule counts 'belajar/learning', which inflates Indonesian beginner counts.
proposal_action: Lead with beginner positioning (guided start, fewer failures).
primary_validation: Pilot with first-time growers; measure first-harvest success rate with vs without guidance.

hypothesis: Age 20-40 is the core age band
key_metrics: {"metric": "explicit self-reported age", "n": 10, "pct": 0.011, "ages_in_20_40": 3, "ages_reported": 8, "note": "Age is not inferred from writing style; only explicit self-reports are counted."}
rationale: Only ~10 records state an age explicitly. Age cannot be inferred from public text without violating the protocol.
proposal_action: Remove '20–40' as an evidence-based claim; present it as an assumption to test.
primary_validation: Age band question in the primary survey.

hypothesis: Indonesia (Java priority) shows active hydroponic discourse
rationale: Active Indonesian-language hydroponic discourse exists at scale (~30.7k customer-voice records, mostly YouTube comments on Indonesian tutorials) with distinct themes (AB mix, DIY paralon builds, heat/rain). Java priority cannot be tested: explicit locations are rare (Java place names in ~180 records). Indonesian volume reflects our Indonesian-first YouTube query design, not national prevalence.
proposal_action: Cite as 'active Indonesian online hydroponic learning community'; do not claim Java market size from this data.
primary_validation: Survey/marketplace data by province; YouTube audience analytics of partner channels.

rationale: No willingness-to-pay can be derived. Price language leans to frugality: 'cheap/murah/DIY' language (~2.3k) far outnumbers premium language (~0.5k); COST is the 2nd most frequent pain; Indonesian price talk centres on DIY component costs (pipes, AB mix, pumps) and start-up capital, and 'I can build it for a fraction' reactions recur. This is a risk signal for a Rp910,000 kit, not a refutation.
proposal_action: Position against DIY total cost + failure cost; offer an entry tier; keep price claims as hypotheses.
primary_validation: Van Westendorp/Gabor-Granger price test; conjoint on kit vs DIY vs media refills.

rationale: Technology talk (sensors/automation/app/AI) appears on all 8 platforms but in only ~4% of records. Explicit monitoring requests exist (~90). Aspect sentiment on sensors is more negative than positive (calibration, reliability), and a passive/no-electronics preference (Kratky, wick) recurs.
proposal_action: Treat 'tech-interested' as a sub-segment; sell outcomes (fewer dead plants) rather than technology.
primary_validation: Concept test: monitoring kit vs guided passive kit preference.

hypothesis: Sustainability interest is a purchase driver
rationale: Sustainability appears in ~7% of records and is positive in <1%; among purchase-signal records ~11% mention sustainability vs ~33% price/cost. Some skepticism (energy use, 'boros listrik'). Sustainability is a secondary value, not a purchase driver, in this corpus.
proposal_action: Keep sustainability as a supporting/brand and competition-theme message; do not make it the primary purchase reason.
primary_validation: Survey ranking of purchase drivers; A/B message test (sustainability vs ease/success).

rationale: School/campus/institution contexts appear in <1% of records. Community and education are, however, the most explicitly requested support features (education ~230 explicit requests on 8 platforms).
proposal_action: Use schools/communities as channels and content partners; keep institutional sales as a hypothesis.

hypothesis: B2B (urban farms, restaurants, hotels, SMEs) is a viable segment
rationale: Commercial/business discourse is present (~2% professional signal; Indonesian 'usaha/modal/jual' talk), but restaurants and hotels are rarely mentioned (B2B context ~0.4%). Small hydroponic businesses discuss monitoring time and capital, which fits an SME tier more than hospitality.
proposal_action: Reframe B2B toward small hydroponic SMEs/farmer groups first; hotels/restaurants as later hypotheses.
primary_validation: B2B discovery interviews with 10 hydroponic SMEs.

hypothesis: Sugarcane bagasse media is customer-relevant value
rationale: Bagasse is almost absent from customer discourse (18 customer-voice mentions out of ~91k). Of 152 bagasse mentions found anywhere, only ~19 are in a growing-media/compost context; most are tableware, packaging, energy or paper. Growers talk about rockwool, coco, perlite, clay pebbles and sponge; rockwool concerns (irritation, pH, waste) appear ~160 times. Bagasse is an engineering/sustainability differentiator, not a value customers currently ask for.
proposal_action: Sell the medium on performance and convenience (germination, no itch, no disposal hassle, local/cheap), with bagasse as the proof of circularity. Prove it works before claiming it.
primary_validation: Lab germination/rooting trials vs rockwool and sponge; blind user trial.

hypothesis: Users want monitoring of pH/EC/TDS/temperature/water level
rationale: pH and TDS/EC monitoring reach EXPLICIT_REQUEST on ≥6 platforms; PH/EC_TDS/NUTRIENTS pains total ~2.5k records with high severity; TDS/PPM meter and calibration is its own topic. Supported by extension guidance and academic literature. Caveats: calibration burden and sensor reliability are recurring complaints.
proposal_action: Make pH + TDS/EC monitoring and 'what to do next' guidance the core value; budget for calibration UX and sensor quality.
primary_validation: Bench test sensor accuracy (target ±0.2 pH as in the team's own plan) and a 4-week home pilot.

hypothesis: Users want AI recommendations / anomaly detection
rationale: Customers rarely ask for 'AI' (explicit AI mentions are few; AI aspect sentiment is split ~22% positive / 23% negative). But the underlying jobs — diagnose what is wrong, tell me what to adjust — are the most frequent pains (PLANT_HEALTH, NUTRIENTS, KNOWLEDGE), and diagnostics is explicitly requested. Demand is for answers, not for AI as such.
proposal_action: Market 'diagnosis and step-by-step fixes'; mention AI as the mechanism, not the benefit.
primary_validation: Wizard-of-Oz test: human-generated recommendations in the app before building ML.

rationale: Subscription mentions (~860) are mostly about proprietary seed pods/refills; explicit dislike of subscriptions/pod lock-in recurs (~20) and app complaints are about connectivity and missing alerts. AeroGarden's 2024 shutdown announcement (expert stream) shows app/brand continuity risk. No evidence of willingness to pay for premium software.
proposal_action: Make the kit fully usable without subscription; monetize consumables that are optional/open (media, nutrients) before software.
primary_validation: Measure 30-day app retention in pilot; test premium feature uptake with a free trial.
